culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: At the Taj Mahal: no eating or smoking inside; tobacco, liquor, food, headphones, knives, chargers, tripods and electric goods other than cameras are banned; phones off or silent; no noise inside the mausoleum; don't touch or scratch the walls. Hire only approved guides and photographers who show ID.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Photography is banned inside the main mausoleum, and drones are banned in and around the Taj Mahal. Polluting vehicles are barred within 500 m.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Uttar Pradesh (official Taj Mahal website).
culture-and-protocol.note: Taj Mahal only. Shoe covers come with the foreigner ticket. Other Uttar Pradesh sites (for example Varanasi ghats) are not covered.

For vehicle visits to protected areas, the state ecotourism guidance says to take an authorised guide in each vehicle and pay the applicable guide fee before entry. Check the particular reserve and current arrangements with the authority.

The state ecotourism guidance says visitors traversing protected areas must show their park entry pass and/or identity proof when a forest official asks. Dudhwa National Park has an online availability and booking page; check the specific reserve and current pass process before travelling.

laws.rule: Uttar Pradesh ecotourism guidance says vehicles traversing protected areas must not exceed 20 km/h and should stay at least 50 metres apart.
In protected areas, the state ecotourism guidance says visitors must keep at least 20 metres from wildlife; if an animal approaches a vehicle, stay still and allow it passage.
The state ecotourism guidance says not to feed, tease or chase animals, bring pets, or throw plastic, bottles, tins or other objects in the park.

On safaris, the state ecotourism guidance says not to leave a vehicle except at authorised places, exceed vehicle capacity, overtake other tourist vehicles, or stay at an animal sighting for more than five minutes.

Uttar Pradesh ecotourism guidance says not to carry arms, explosives or intoxicants into parks; do not play music or shout while on safari, and switch off mobile phones and reversing horns during core-area safaris.
